# Implementation Readiness Checklist: Synthia Platform Engineering Scaffold

**Purpose**: Validate that the revised plan specifies each engineering area well enough to implement
from — before Stage 1 begins.
**Created**: 2026-09-15
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md) · [plan.md](../plan.md) · Constitution v3.1.0

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does **not** mean implementation work is complete.

> **This checklist does not certify that anything is built.** Every item asks whether a requirement is
> *specified well enough to build from*, never whether code works. **Part A** covers the scaffold
> (Stages 1–13). **Part B** covers the twelve business use cases (Stage 14), which are deliberately
> undefined — Part B is expected to be largely unsatisfiable today, and that is the correct result.
> No new architecture is proposed here.

---

## A7. Persistence

- [x] CHK034 Is it specified **which** entities require soft delete, rather than "where required"? [Ambiguity, Plan Stage 7]
  - *Closed 2026-09-16.* `data-model.md` §Conventions now states plainly: **no entity in the scaffold soft-deletes, and none is intended to.** Erasure is a hard delete because a soft-deleted row is still the organisation's data and a flag would defeat FR-AUDIT-006; retention is a removal, not a flag. The convention is reserved, with the rule that the first table to adopt it says why there. T104 updated.
- [x] CHK035 Are the specific invariant transactions that justify Serializable isolation named, rather than left as a category? [Ambiguity, Plan Stage 7]
  - *Closed 2026-09-16.* `data-model.md` §Conventions now states **no Serializable transaction exists in the scaffold** and names how each invariant is held instead — the conditional claim on `claimed_at IS NULL`, the unique `work_item_id` on `approval`, the `idempotency_key` primary key, the unique `(message_id, given_by_oid)`. A future Serializable transaction must be named there first. T104 updated.
- [x] CHK036 Are the standard audit columns enumerated, so every table applies the same set? [Completeness, Data model §Conventions]
- [x] CHK037 Is the view-versioning rule specified with the prohibition on in-place alteration, not only the convention to add a version? [Clarity, Contracts §read-views]
- [x] CHK038 Is the EF-migration conflict with ADR-0001/0003 stated where an implementer will encounter it, with the condition for resolving it? [Conflict, Plan §Recorded conflict]
- [x] CHK039 Are optimistic-concurrency requirements specified for every mutable entity, including the newest three? [Coverage, Data model §Conventions]
  - *Closed 2026-09-16.* `idempotency_record` is now the **single named exemption**, stated both in §Conventions and on the entity: the primary key already serialises every concurrent writer, so the row structurally cannot have two live writers and a `version` column would be a second mechanism for a race that cannot occur. Every other table carries `version`, and a further exemption must be named. T098 and T104 updated.

## A8. Messaging

- [x] CHK040 Is the outbox specified as a behavioural requirement anywhere, or only as a plan-level and data-model decision? [Traceability, Gap]
- [x] CHK041 Are outbox dispatch semantics specified — ordering guarantees, retry, and what happens to a permanently undispatchable row? [Coverage, Gap]
  - *Closed 2026-09-16.* `contracts/triggers.md` gains **§Dispatcher obligations — before the message exists**: a ceiling of 10 attempts with exponential backoff and jitter, no blocked row blocking another, the row marked undispatchable and left in place rather than dropped, and — for a `granted` kind — surfaced in `vw_approval_unexecuted_v1` as a **governance** failure with recovery by fresh authorization, never replay. Rationale recorded: past fifteen minutes a retry can no longer produce a valid execution, so it would only manufacture pending work that can never complete. T115 updated.
- [x] CHK042 Is the trigger payload constraint stated as an exhaustive allow-list rather than a list of prohibited fields? [Clarity, Contracts §triggers]
- [x] CHK043 Are the two idempotency boundaries specified as both required, with neither substituting for the other? [Consistency, Data model]
- [x] CHK044 Is dead-letter handling specified as a product-visible outcome, not only an operational one? [Completeness, Plan Stage 8]

## A11. Observability

- [x] CHK055 Is correlation specified end to end — accepted, generated, echoed, bound, and carried onto triggers and audit? [Completeness, Plan Stage 10]
- [x] CHK056 Are telemetry sampling and retention specified, or left to implementation discretion? [Gap]
  - *Closed 2026-09-16.* **FR-OPS-011** sets telemetry retention at 30 days against audit's 7 years — which is what makes FR-OPS-004 true in practice rather than only by policy. **FR-OPS-012** requires sampling to be decided per correlated journey, prohibiting any strategy that could keep a journey's request half and discard its resume half. Plan Stage 10 names tail-based sampling keyed on the correlation identifier, with errors, denials and approvals always retained. New task T142a.

## A14. Angular standards

- [x] CHK070 Are the library boundaries specified with the import rules that enforce them? [Measurability, Plan Stage 3]
- [x] CHK071 Is "role gating is presentation only" stated together with the requirement that the server re-decides? [Completeness, Spec §FR-SURF-004]
- [x] CHK072 Are CSP and sanitization requirements specified concretely enough to review, rather than named as policies? [Clarity, Constitution §Angular]
  - *Closed 2026-09-16.* Plan Stage 3 gains a **concrete CSP baseline** — full directive set, delivered as a response header rather than a `<meta>` tag so injected markup cannot strip it, with `connect-src` limited to the single gateway origin, the SignalR endpoint and the Entra authority, and `frame-ancestors 'none'`, `base-uri 'none'`, `object-src 'none'`. *Amended 2026-09-19: `base-uri` is `'self'`. Sent against the real build for the first time, `'none'` blocked the `<base href="/">` every Angular document carries, on all three surfaces — see plan Stage 3 for the evidence and for why the alternative costs more.* Stage 4 applies the same baseline to the renderer from the main process. Recorded why `script-src` excludes `'unsafe-eval'`: the build is AOT precisely so it can. T048 and T054 updated.

## A15. Electron security

- [x] CHK074 Are all the mandatory switches enumerated with the meaning of "where compatible" for sandbox? [Ambiguity, Plan Stage 4]
  - *Closed 2026-09-16.* Resolved rather than left discretionary: **`sandbox=true` is unconditional in this scaffold**, because the one thing that breaks sandbox — a preload needing Node built-ins — does not apply to a preload that exposes a narrow typed bridge and nothing else. Disabling it now requires an ADR. T050 updated.
- [x] CHK075 Is IPC validation specified for **both** sender and arguments, as two distinct obligations? [Completeness, Constitution P-VII]
- [x] CHK076 Is the `contextBridge` surface specified as an allow-list, so a reviewer can tell whether an addition is permitted? [Clarity, Plan Stage 4]
- [x] CHK077 Is the navigation allow-list specified, rather than the restriction merely asserted? [Gap]
  - *Closed 2026-09-16.* Plan Stage 4 gains the **complete navigation allow-list**: the renderer bundle origin, the single gateway origin, and the Entra authority. The window-open handler denies every destination without exception, an external link goes to `shell.openExternal` only after the same check, and scheme matching is exact on HTTPS/WSS — never `http:`, `file:` or a custom scheme. T053 updated.
- [x] CHK078 Is "no business authorization in the renderer **or** main process" stated for both, since only one is the usual mistake? [Consistency, Constitution P-VII]

## A16. Container and runtime

- [x] CHK079 Is the digest-update process defined, rather than only required to be documented? [Gap, Plan Stage 10]
  - *Closed 2026-09-16.* Plan Stage 10 now **defines** the digest-update process rather than requiring it be documented: named owner, three triggers (High/Critical CVE, monthly schedule, base-image runtime release), a scheduled CI job that opens a PR with the vulnerability diff, and a gate of full suite plus clean image scan — a digest never reaches production on a green scan alone. Emergency path may skip the schedule but not the gate. New task T148a.
- [x] CHK080 Are health endpoint semantics specified so readiness cannot silently become a liveness copy? [Clarity, Plan Stage 10]
- [x] CHK081 Are resource limits specified per deployable, or only required to be explicit? [Gap]
- [x] CHK082 Is the 25-second drain specified with the behaviour of in-flight work during scale-in? [Coverage, Gap]
  - *Closed 2026-09-16.* Plan Stage 10 states drain is a **grace period, not a guarantee**, and resolves the collision with FR-EXEC-006: pre-claim, the message returns to the queue and the atomic claim absorbs the duplicate; **post-claim, work outliving the drain surfaces as approved-but-not-executed** per ADR-0002 and recovers only by fresh authorization, never a re-fire. Yields a scheduling rule — drain must exceed the longest single external call, which is why every outbound call has an explicit timeout. T148 updated.
- [x] CHK083 Is the read-only root filesystem stated as a requirement or a preference, and is any write path identified? [Ambiguity, Constitution §Containers]

## A17. Testing

- [x] CHK084 Are all fifteen test categories mapped to at least one stage, with none left to "wherever it fits"? [Coverage, Plan Stage 11]
- [x] CHK085 Is it specified which change triggers which test category, so the obligation is actionable? [Clarity, Gap]
  - *Closed 2026-09-16.* Constitution **v3.1.0** adds the change-type → owed-category mapping. Same fix closes `architecture.md` CHK065.
- [x] CHK086 Is the hard-failure gate specified as "each protection has a test that fails when the protection is removed"? [Measurability, Plan Stage 11]
- [x] CHK087 Are coverage expectations specified, or deliberately excluded? [Gap]
  - *Closed 2026-09-16.* Constitution **v3.1.0** adds §Coverage, recording the position explicitly: **no threshold is set and none gates a merge**, deliberately. The gate is behavioural — the required categories plus a failing-then-passing test for every Principle VIII hard failure. A percentage would be satisfiable without any of that. Coverage may be measured as information; making it a gate requires an amendment.
- [x] CHK088 Are the golden-path acceptance conditions specified precisely enough to judge pass or fail without interpretation? [Measurability, Plan Stages 12–13]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit-specify` and `/speckit-clarify`
- Part B is expected to be almost entirely unchecked until product definitions arrive; that is the
  designed outcome, not an outstanding defect
- Items marked `[Gap]` were identified by inspecting the current artifacts; they are starting points
  for review, not confirmed defects
- Add findings inline beneath an item rather than editing the item text
